post.description:
Check that I may act in a workspace and remember it for my next sign-in; any other id is not found.

The browser tab then names it in X-Workspace-Id on each request. Requests without that header (other tabs of an older
panel, scripts on the cookie) keep the workspace the session started in, so a switch here never redirects them.

get.description: The workspaces I belong to, my own first, with my role in each.

post.description: Probe one domain again now; a read-only check, so an operator may run it.

delete.description: Undo an acknowledgement: the issue counts and alerts again.

post.description: Acknowledge a current issue: it stays listed but is not counted or sent to Telegram until the ack ends.

get.description: Every issue that was active during the range, with how often and how long, and each separate occurrence.

post.description: A key that acts only inside the current workspace.

get.description:
Bytes each server exchanged with each peer server in a window (hour resolution), biggest first.

With `category` (an id or 'none') only links where the server or its peer is in that category.

post.description:
Add a person by their numeric Telegram id; they sign in with Telegram and see this workspace next to their own.

Only the panel owner (owner of workspace 1) adds people: every new member can sign in and gets a workspace, so this
is the registration door of the panel. The answer is the membership only, never the person's profile.

delete.description: Take a person out of this workspace; their own workspace and other memberships stay as they are.

get.description: The whole fleet over time: traffic summed over every server, usage averaged, how many reported.
Per server percent of time reporting, from gaps between reports and offline incidents (default 7 days).
One compact fleet briefing for an AI assistant to read first. format=md is the dense text, detail=full lifts the caps.
Peak-hour CPU, steal, load, conntrack and RAM per server, sibling comparison and growth (default 7 days).
The change log of the current workspace, newest first, at most 500 events (default last 24 h).
The digest: the last 24 h (or since..until) against the equal window before it.
A 0-100 score and band per server, with the penalties and hard gates that fired and the signals not measured yet.
Incident counts by code and server, MTTR, flapping issues and the longest outages (default 7 days).
Every fix guide (code, title, detector live or planned) plus the standing operating rules.
Likely causes, read-only checks, safe fixes and never-do rules for an issue code (ping:<ip> works); unknown codes get the generic guide.
Relay-by-exit matrix of loss, RTT and a path verdict, plus bytes per pair (default 7 days for bytes).
Fleet and per-server bytes, peak day and hour, relay-exit pair bytes (default 7 days).
Everything an AI agent needs about the current workspace in one secret-free JSON document.

post.description:
A chat the shared bot may post this workspace's alerts to, checked with Telegram before it is saved.

A group or channel: the bot must be an administrator that may post, and so must one of this workspace's owner or
admins. A private chat (a positive id): only one of those people's own id. One chat belongs to one workspace.
Send one message through the bot; the bot token never leaves the server.

get.description:
Traffic over time for a window [since, until) or a preset range (24h, 7d, 30d, 90d), with the busiest days and hours.

Hourly buckets for windows up to 8 days, daily ones beyond, aligned to the UTC offset. Without server_id: the whole fleet.

Traffic per server and for the fleet (only one category when `category` is an id or 'none') over a window [since, until) in unix seconds (default: the last 30 days).

Always today and yesterday; for the window the total, daily average, peak day and share of the fleet.
Days are local days at the UTC offset in minutes (default +03:30) and the window is counted in whole days (at most 366).
Download is rx (into the server), upload is tx (out of it).
